decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location Plan UC-0310-PBP Proposed Block PlanUC-2012-EPSEUC-2212-EPGFPUC-2212-EPESUC-1807-EPPFlood Risk Assessment, Flood Warning and Evacuation Plan and Surface Water Drainage Strategy: AEG7559_N18_London_07 dated 24/11/2025Environmental Noise Impact Assessment PREPARED by Dr Haydar Aygun dated: 11/01/2026Energy Statement 13/09/2024 by info@vision-energy.co.uk dated 13/09/2024Archaeological Desk-Based Assessment by border archaeology dated November 2024Fire Statement by ADA Group Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.
The external finishing materials shall match those used in the construction of the existing building and/or areas of hard surfacing. Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance.

Prior to occupation of the development, a Verification Report demonstrating that the approved SuDS and Flood Risk measures AEG7559_N18_London_07 24th November 2025) have been fully implemented shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. This report must include:As built drawings of the sustainable drainage systems including level information (if appropriate).Photographs of the completed sustainable drainage systems.Any relevant certificates from manufacturers/ suppliers of any drainage features.A confirmation statement of the above signed by the site manager or similar.Reason : To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD 59, 60 61 and 62 of the Development Managment Document (2014) and Policies SI12 and SI13 of the London Plan (2021) and the NPPF (2024).

Prior to occupation, unless otherwise agreed cycle parking should be provided in compliance with the following criteria:Provision of a minimum of TWO long stay cycle parking spaces in an accessible location: the access route to the cycle parking enclosures should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike to enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door) which must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2m.Long stay must be secured: with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob.Long stay must be fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roof. Reason: The Council's Climate Action and Transport Policies seek to increase the use of active and sustainable transport modes. This means that access to bicycle parking should be easy and secure to remove potential barriers to cycling

Prior to first occupation details of the design of refuse storage facilities including facilities for the recycling of waste shall be provided within the development, in accordance with the London Borough of Enfield - Waste and Recycling Planning Storage Guidance ENV 08/162.In particular, waste collection vehicles must be able to get within 25m of the refuse storage point.Reason: In order to facilitate efficient, safe and clean removal of refuse, the location and accessibility of refuse storage plus to maintain safety on the Highway.
